pages.text: [#](53341a)The heart of every working — a cauldron of water over a steady fire.[#]()
[#](53341a)A heated cauldron full of water is a patient thing. It takes whatever you give it, in the order you give it, and remembers.[#]()
pages.title: Brewing in the Cauldron

pages.text: [#](53341a)Light a fire beneath it and fill the bowl. Drop your reagents in one at a time. When the brew suits you, dip an empty bottle and draw it off.[#]()
[#](53341a)Some things you add are not the brew, but a hand laid upon it. **Glowstone** makes the next working stronger; **redstone** makes it last.[#]()
pages.title: A Hand Upon the Brew

pages.text: [#](53341a)A **fermented spider eye** turns a kindness into a cruelty, or back again. Lay these *before* the reagent they shape — the cauldron remembers only forward.[#]()
[#](53341a)The reagent decides the gift: a spider's eye for poison, sugar for swiftness, a ghast's tear for mending, wormwood for unseeing.[#]()
pages.title: The Gift of the Reagent

pages.text: [#](53341a)**Gunpowder** bursts the bottle where it lands, sharing its work with all nearby. **Dragon's breath** leaves a slow, drifting fog. With neither, the draught is yours alone.[#]()
[#](53341a)Eight reagents at most before the water grows too muddled. Pour off what you have made, rinse with fresh water, and begin the next working.[#]()
pages.title: Knowing When to Stop
